subject: Demo — confirm meeting time and UTC offsets around US clock change
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: julia.park@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-10-30T13:14:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — multi-region team availability

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this — we'd love a 45-min walkthrough of Redwood Inference next week. Our team is split across London, San Francisco and Bangalore, so timezone clarity is important. A few proposed slots (all listed as local times below):

- Tue Nov 2, 11:00 London (CET)
- Wed Nov 3, 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET
- Thu Nov 4, 19:30 IST

Two quick notes:
1) The US daylight saving time change is on Sunday Nov 7 this year — if you propose times the week after, please confirm the UTC offsets (PT/PDT, ET/EDT) explicitly.
2) We prefer a Zoom link and a short agenda. Attaching a short wish-list of topics.

Would appreciate a confirm on the best slot (and explicit offsets) so I can send invites to our folks.

Cheers,
Sam Turner
Director of Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
Attachments: acme_questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet of topics)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-30T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — multi-region team availability

Sam — thanks, this is helpful. We're flexible; to avoid any ambiguity around the Nov 7 US clock change, below are two clean options that explicitly state UTC offsets for the date in question. Please pick the one that works for your group.

Option A (before US DST ends):
- Wed Nov 3, 08:00 PT (PDT, UTC-7) / 11:00 ET (EDT, UTC-4) / 16:00 UTC / 17:00 CET / 21:30 IST — 45 minutes

Option B (after US DST ends):
- Tue Nov 9, 10:00 PT (PST, UTC-8) / 13:00 ET (EST, UTC-5) / 18:00 UTC / 19:00 CET / 23:30 IST — 45 minutes

Notes:
- We recommend Option B if your EU/IN folks prefer a post-DST schedule (US clocks change on Sun Nov 7).
- I'll attach a one-page agenda (see redwood_demo_agenda.pdf) and include Aditya for security/compliance Qs.
- When we confirm a time I'll send an ICS with all times written out as: PT (UTC-8), ET (UTC-5), UTC, CET, IST — so calendar clients don't mis-interpret.

Zoom link provisional: https://zoom.us/j/1234567890?pwd=demo

Would you like me to provision a calendar invite for Option B (Tue Nov 9) at the times above?

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_demo_agenda.pdf

Looping in a quick note — I'm available for Option B (Nov 9) and can cover the platform roadmap section. Aditya — can you join the tail of the session for the security checklist? If so I'll include you on the invite.

Laura Bennett

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-01T11:05:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — multi-region team availability

Thanks Jonas — Option B should work for most. One small concern: when you say "PT (PST, UTC-8)" and "ET (EST, UTC-5)" can you confirm those offsets apply on Nov 9 (i.e., after the Nov 7 change)? We want to make sure calendar clients show the correct hour for folks in San Francisco (we had a bad recurring invite once where a DST mismatch shifted the meeting by an hour).

Also: can the invite include both the named timezone (PT / ET) and the explicit UTC offsets in parentheses as the event title/description? That helps our calendar admins when generating cross-tenant invites.

Sam

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-02T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — multi-region team availability

Sam — great question and totally valid concern. Confirming explicitly for the record:

For a meeting scheduled on Tue Nov 9, 2027 we will use the post-DST (standard) offsets:
- 10:00 PT (PST, UTC-8)
- 13:00 ET (EST, UTC-5)
- 18:00 UTC
- 19:00 CET (CET, UTC+1)
- 23:30 IST (IST, UTC+5:30)

I'll create the calendar invite for Tue Nov 9 at 10:00 PT and include the explicit offsets in both the event title and description, e.g.:
"Redwood Inference demo — Nov 9, 10:00 PT (PST, UTC-8) / 13:00 ET (EST, UTC-5) / 18:00 UTC"

I'll attach the SOW draft and the questionnaire you sent to the invite as well. Zoom link will be the one below. If anyone on your side prefers a browser-forward ICS instead of an attached .ics file, let me know and I can add both.

Final calendar details (to be sent in invite):
- When: Tue Nov 9, 2027 — 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET / 18:00 UTC
- Length: 45 minutes
- Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/1234567890?pwd=demo
- Materials: redwood_demo_agenda.pdf, sow_draft.docx, acme_questionnaire.xlsx

See you then — and we'll make sure the invite displays both named zones and UTC offsets to avoid any client misinterpretation.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
